facts.claim: Google's Drive MCP server is https://drivemcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1 (streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.0).
facts.evidence: Reference page and setup guide give the endpoint; the protected-resource document at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/v1 names the same resource.

facts.claim: Setup uses a manually created OAuth client (id and secret); no dynamic client registration is offered.
facts.evidence: Guide: 'Create an OAuth client' and add it to the MCP client; accounts.google.com metadata has no registration_endpoint.

facts.claim: Google's guide lists the scopes drive.readonly and drive.file; the protected-resource document also offers the full drive scope.
facts.evidence: Guide scopes list; protected-resource scopes_supported [drive, drive.readonly, drive.file].

facts.claim: The authorization server is accounts.google.com (authorize) with the token endpoint at oauth2.googleapis.com; lotr discovery resolves them.
facts.evidence: authorization_endpoint accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth, token_endpoint oauth2.googleapis.com/token; lotrlib.oauth.discover (GET only) resolved issuer https://accounts.google.com and both hosts.

facts.claim: Tools: copy_file, create_file, download_file_content, get_file_metadata, get_file_permissions, list_recent_files, read_file_content, search_files.
facts.evidence: Both the reference page and the setup guide list the same eight tools (same site; read/write split inferred from names).

facts.claim: Prerequisites: Google Workspace Developer Preview Program membership, a Google Cloud project, the Drive API and Drive MCP API enabled, an OAuth consent screen.
facts.evidence: Prerequisites and steps on the guide (last updated 2026-10-09).

facts.claim: Google issues a refresh token when the authorization request carries access_type=offline (prompt=consent makes it re-issue one on a repeat sign-in); offline_access is not a Google scope.
facts.evidence: Guide: set access_type to offline to get a refresh token; prompt=consent to re-prompt. accounts.google.com metadata scopes_supported has no offline_access.

choices.decision: mcp-oauth-preregistered against Google's hosted Drive MCP
choices.because: Official hosted MCP that publishes RFC 9728 metadata but needs your own OAuth client.
The scopes Google's guide lists; the full drive scope is not needed.

choices.decision: offline_access false, auth_params access_type=offline and prompt=consent
choices.because: Google gives refresh tokens through access_type=offline, not the offline_access scope (which lotr would add to the scope list).

choices.decision: explicit read for read_file_content and download_file_content; create_file and copy_file write
choices.because: Names do not start with get_/list_/search, so they would otherwise be classed as writes.

open: auth_params access_type=offline + prompt=consent have not been tried against a live Google sign-in; that Google then returns a refresh token rests on Google's OAuth guide.
Whether Google's authorization endpoint accepts the RFC 8707 resource parameter was not tested; if it refuses, set send_resource false.

Google's guide shows a Web application client with hosted redirect URIs; its web-server guide exempts localhost and loopback-IP redirect URIs from the https rule, but a client registered with http://127.0.0.1:8977/callback has not been tried.
Arguments of list_recent_files (smoke op) are not stated; assumed optional.
Read/write tiers for the eight tools are inferred from names; Google publishes no annotations on the reference page.
